name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Run the kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript tool on the first pending vid. This gives us a clean, machine-readable transcript immediately, which the Creative team can repurpose into reels, blogs, or social snippets without manual retyping. The trade-off is that we skip human review for typos or tone—accept that risk to move faster.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t typos—it’s losing control of the narrative. If we automate transcripts without human review, we risk amplifying errors that shape our brand voice. Instead, assign the Creative team to spot-check the first 10% of transcripts manually before full automation; if error rates stay below 2%, expand. That settles it.

name: Chisel
text:
Product Ops should enforce a *mandatory, timestamped, module-level review* of every automated transcript before Creative repurposes it. This prevents brand-damaging errors from slipping into public content while keeping the speed gain from automation. The trade-off is a small delay in publishing, but it’s worth it to protect narrative control.
[dispatched 4 workers: worker-8349, worker-3101, worker-9011… — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t just brand voice—it’s liability. If an automated transcript misquotes a guest or omits a critical disclaimer, we’re exposed to legal challenges. Instead, Legal should draft a *standardized review checklist* for Creative to apply before repurposing, with Product Ops enforcing it. Settle this by having Legal sign off on the checklist within 48 hours.
